clue.text: Sick and tired of being given haute cuisine?

definitions.meaning: weary and exasperated, having had enough of something
jokingly, fed in an upmarket way, served high-class food

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling that they are weary of endless fine dining.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having had enough, and the second reading splits it as eaten well at the top end of the market.

clue.text: Retire now that autumn has returned

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
back means returned, as in came back

explanation.surface: Someone deciding to withdraw from work as the leaves come down.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall back is to withdraw or retreat, as troops do.

clue.text: Follows the sailor and the sailor follows it

parts.note: dogs means follows closely, as in dogs someone's footsteps
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman who trails a star across the sky while it trails him.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase 'the sailor' appears twice: the first gives TAR, the second begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius is a bright star that seafarers have long steered by.

clue.text: Pious, sober cabinet-maker under George III

parts.note: pi is short slang for pious
TT means teetotal, so sober

explanation.surface: A devout, abstemious furniture craftsman working in the reign of George III.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet-maker' pretends to be a carpenter; it means a Prime Minister who formed a cabinet, William Pitt the Younger.
explanation.definitionFit: William Pitt the Younger was Prime Minister under George III and so assembled his ministers.

clue.text: A brief examination as soon as completed

parts.note: once can mean as soon as, as in 'once it's done'
over means finished or completed

explanation.surface: A quick inspection carried out the moment a job is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick look over something is a cursory inspection.

clue.text: Fowler needs to take in a prolonged search dating from 1066

parts.note: Norman Fowler was a Conservative cabinet minister
con means deceive, take in
a quest is a long search

explanation.surface: A bird-catcher must hunt at length for something dating back to 1066.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fowler' looks like a bird-catcher; it is Sir Norman Fowler, a British Conservative politician of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Normandy invaded England in 1066, the year of that conquest.

clue.text: Whence Napoleon was able to go back

indicators.note: go back says the word able is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: The island from which Napoleon managed to return to France.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was exiled to Elba and escaped from there in 1815.

clue.text: A rogue from Illinois caught in vain

indicators.note: caught in says the abbreviation is held inside the following word

parts.note: ILL is an abbreviation for the US state of Illinois

explanation.surface: A crook from Illinois arrested, all to no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a scoundrel or criminal.

clue.text: A sovereign state!

parts.note: a kingdom, a domain ruled over by a monarch, with the exclamation hinting at the sovereign as a ruler not a coin

explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is the territory ruled by a sovereign.

clue.text: A whisky induced assault by a fiery debater?

definitions.text: A whisky induced assault by a fiery debater?

parts.words: A whisky induced assault by a fiery debater?
parts.note: an assault fuelled by drink, and also a lively verbal onslaught from a passionate speaker

explanation.definitionFit: A lively, vigorous offensive, with drink playing on the alcohol sense of spirits.

clue.text: Have a cigarette and become cheerful

definitions.meaning: to start smoking by setting tobacco alight

explanation.surface: A smoker cheered by lighting a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting tobacco and a brightening face both use this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Massage the Spanish, the French, and the German measles

parts.note: rub means massage
el is Spanish for the
la is French for the

explanation.surface: A rubdown given to Spanish, French and German patients with a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the German' looks like a third foreign article in the list, but 'German measles' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: German measles is the common name for this mild viral infection.

clue.text: Computer units that mechanics chuck in

definitions.meaning: binary digits, the smallest units of data
drill pieces clamped in the chuck of a drill

explanation.surface: Engineers throwing computer parts away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chuck in' looks like throwing in; a chuck is the clamp of a drill that holds the bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Binary digits are the smallest data units, and drill tips are fitted into a chuck.

clue.text: Advertisement urging avoidance of spirit from the wood?

parts.note: dry describes a campaign or place that bans alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A temperance poster warning against drink matured in the cask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the wood' suggests beer drawn from the barrel; the definition is a creature from the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree nymph in Greek myth lives in woodland.

clue.text: West to prepare for hostilities to hot up

parts.note: to arm is to get ready for war

explanation.surface: The West readying itself for conflict as tension rises.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat is to make or become less cold.

clue.text: Well I never act in loco parentis!

definitions.meaning: to take a father's place, read as two words

explanation.surface: Astonishment at being asked to stand in as a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish exclamation is also BE DAD, play the father, which is acting in loco parentis (Latin, in place of a parent).
explanation.definitionFit: It is a mild Irish oath meaning 'by God', an expression of surprise.

clue.text: Doctor takes tea or coffee

parts.note: MO is medical officer, an army doctor
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A GP choosing between a cuppa and a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variety of fine coffee, originally shipped from Yemen.

clue.text: Latest report on a river bank deposit

parts.note: current means latest or present-day
an account is a report or narrative

explanation.surface: The newest news about a river's edge being silted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a river' and 'bank' dress the surface as geography, with current as flow; the definition is the everyday banking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque account is where money is placed with a bank for everyday use.

clue.text: Where a milkman is employed when avoiding the police

explanation.surface: A milkman doing his round while dodging the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery round is a run, and a fugitive is said to be fleeing in this idiom.

clue.text: Where holidayers could build sand huts in line

indicators.note: build says the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Tourists building a row of sandcastles on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny island is a typical holiday destination, and the title of a Harry Belafonte song.

clue.text: Handy coal store for cooking cutlets

indicators.note: cooking suggests the meat is being reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A convenient fuel bin beside the stove where chops are fried.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal bucket for coal kept by the fireplace.

clue.text: Leave house for a few minutes with underwear showing

definitions.text: Leave house for a few minutes

definitions.meaning: a petticoat peeping out below a hem

explanation.surface: Popping out of the house with a petticoat on view.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip out briefly, and a petticoat that has come into view.

clue.text: Block tobacco advert.

explanation.surface: A tobacco advertisement being banned.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopper, a cake of chewing tobacco and a promotional mention all share the word.

clue.text: Eye-opening term for a scholar

explanation.surface: A revelatory word for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hole in the iris and a student both bear the name.

clue.text: Ale with plenty of body

explanation.surface: Beer that is full-bodied.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark beer and a plump physique share this word.

clue.text: Kiss from lisping circle of friends

indicators.note: a lisp turns the hissing sound into a soft th, so the word kiss is said that way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A peck on the cheek from someone with a speech impediment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lisping' changes the SS of KISS to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phrase 'kith and kin', it means friends and acquaintances.

clue.text: Sound floor has a defect

indicators.note: sound says the next word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A solid floor turns out to be faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, floor and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A fault or imperfection.

clue.text: He refuses to go out in a small taxi

parts.note: cab is another word for taxi

explanation.surface: Someone declining to go out for the evening, sitting in a little taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' means strike: the answer is a worker who refuses to join a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike-breaker who will not walk out with his colleagues.

clue.text: Hors d'oeuvre everyone upset on knee

parts.note: pâté is a starter

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the word for everyone is written backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A starter spilt over everyone's lap.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is the bone at the front of the knee.

clue.text: Help an outspoken sucker

indicators.note: outspoken says the next word is to be spoken aloud

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Assistance for a gullible person who speaks frankly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid or relief given in difficulty.

clue.text: Misinform a funeral vigil and don't sleep

parts.note: to lie is to misinform
taken as written
a wake is a watch kept over the dead

explanation.surface: Telling fibs at a wake and staying up all night.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain conscious in bed through the night.

clue.text: Don't declare to the staff

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to continue batting instead of closing the innings

explanation.surface: An instruction to colleagues to keep something undisclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain may declare, ending the innings early; to bat on is to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod or stick, and the cricket idiom for carrying on batting.
